races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Race

runners_data.name: Bold Style
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator for Andrew Slattery, Ben Coen takes the ride — 178 days off the track is a significant fitness concern, and while similar-going form reads adequately (6/9 runners, zero wins), this horse needs a well-run race to deliver its best late.
runners_data.comment: Already proven over today's trip, Bold Style rates the one to beat on our figures despite a moderate recent sequence of two sixths sandwiching two unplaced efforts; a 178-day absence since his latest outing is the only concern.

runners_data.name: Loughrea
runners_data.note: Slattery trains and rides, bringing a sharp 17-day turnaround and a recent win at 8f on Good that is directly relevant; in truth a front-running or prominent type by nature, but the presence of Res Ipsa means she is unlikely to lead and will need to settle just off the pace to factor.
runners_data.comment: Loughrea won last time out and ran to a similar level when second on his prior start, a progressive profile sharpened by a quick 17-day turnaround with today's trip already proven. He rates our third-best here, so has a shade to find on figures, but is firmly in the mix.

runners_data.name: Res Ipsa
runners_data.note: Colin Keane for G M Lyons — the race's confirmed pace-setter with a win and a place from three starts at 8f on Good, and she sets up this race for herself by dictating an uncontested tempo; at 3yo and 135lbs she is the pivotal tactical horse in this small field.
runners_data.comment: Res Ipsa won last time out and was placed on his prior outing, form that comes with today's trip already covered, though a 33-day absence is worth noting. Our figures pitch him below his official mark, leaving him fourth on our numbers.

runners_data.name: Straight Up
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan for Aidan O'Brien, a hold-up horse who has shown the ability to place at 8f on both Good and Soft — the 64-day absence is worth monitoring and her similar-going record (0 wins, 0 places from 2 runs) is underwhelming, but she is best served if the pace is genuinely contested.
runners_data.comment: Straight Up won earlier in this campaign and has today's trip covered, so there is clear ability here, but he was only fifth last time and returns from a 64-day break. He rates our second-best and is one of the leading dangers if back to form.

runners_data.name: Mai Dahlia
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle for Joseph O'Brien brings a hot yard and a red-hot jockey, plus the best recent form string in the field (3-2-1); a prominent racer who is in excellent current form and gets on well with Good turf at 8f, she is the most naturally suited to slot in behind Res Ipsa and strike at the right moment.
runners_data.comment: Mai Dahlia won last time out just 9 days ago and was runner-up two starts back, with her trainer in good form. She's rated bottom of this line-up on our figures, though, making her the one to prove wrong rather than side with.

races.paceDynamic: Res Ipsa is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only five runners and no genuine challenger willing to press from the front, she should be able to roll forward and control a measured, sustainable gallop over this mile at Killarney. Mai Dahlia and Loughrea both carry prominent profiles but, with Res Ipsa already occupying that lead role, one or both will need to settle slightly further back than ideal — Loughrea in particular is a natural prominent racer who is most likely to push up and challenge Res Ipsa for the front, with Mai Dahlia the next most likely to secure a handy position. Bold Style and Straight Up are genuine hold-up types who will be doing their best work late, but a single uncontested pace-setter over a mile on good turf rarely generates the frantic early splits needed to set up a strong closing surge. This race shape firmly favours horses who can race prominently or just behind the leader and quicken in the straight, rather than deep closers who depend on a truly run race to close the gap.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Res Ipsa Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Res Ipsa bowls along uncontested in front at a fair but manageable tempo, dictating from pillar to post.
scenarios.body: She sets a rhythm that suits herself perfectly, and with no rival committed to pushing her early, she can conserve energy before quickening in the straight; her recent back-to-back placed efforts at 8f on Good ground confirm this trip and surface suit her well.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Disrupts Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Loughrea aggressively contests the lead with Res Ipsa and the two burn each other off, lifting the tempo for a furlong or two.
scenarios.body: A contested early pace raises the overall pace shape and drains the front-runners more quickly, bringing the hold-up types into the equation; Straight Up, who handles good ground and has placed at this trip, would be best placed to pick up the pieces late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finishers Swamp Them
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves deceptively strong throughout and the field strings out, leaving the back-markers with a clear run and enough real estate to close.
scenarios.body: Bold Style and Straight Up, both genuine hold-up types, would relish this scenario, though the small field makes a perfectly timed late run harder to execute without a truly pressured pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos Reigns
scenarios.trigger: If Res Ipsa is taken on hard early, fades abruptly, and the field bunches in a slow-run scramble up the straight.
scenarios.body: In a muddled contest with no clear tactical advantage, the highest-rated runner with the most adaptable jockey stands to gain; Mai Dahlia's consistent placed record at 8f on Good suggests she can handle a tactical race.

watchPoints.text: Res Ipsa is the pace-maker and her ability to control the tempo uncontested is the single biggest factor shaping this race — watch how quickly Colin Keane sends her to the front leaving the stalls.
Loughrea's natural instinct is to race prominently and she may push up to challenge Res Ipsa early; if Slattery elects to press the leader, the pace dynamic changes sharply for all runners behind.
Bold Style has not run in 178 days and, while the handicapper rates her at OR 105, any lack of match fitness will blunt what is already a style that demands a truly run race to produce a late burst.

Mai Dahlia's connections — McMonagle and Joseph O'Brien — are in sharp form (14 winners from 53 in 14 days) and she arrives on a nine-day turnaround following a win, so watch whether she is sent forward to cover her rival's pace or asked to sit and quicken.

The going is listed as unknown across all Killarney announcements — if the ground is riding softer than Good in practice, monitor the horses with a "hg:t" headgear flag (Res Ipsa, Mai Dahlia) as this could subtly affect their stride patterns in the straight.

races.name: SIS Supporting Irish Racing Handicap

runners_data.name: Red Autumn
runners_data.note: D K Weld's hold-up filly has genuine good-ground form (2nd over 8f on soft), but steps back to a mile from 9f on 39 days off; needs a strong pace to deliver her finishing run and this scenario may not provide it.|
runners_data.comment: Red Autumn was runner-up four starts back and has stayed competitive since, with form over today's trip already banked. Yet to score in her last five starts, she nonetheless heads our figures here, though a 39-day gap since her latest run is a mild concern.

runners_data.name: Johnny Soda
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter for Adrian McGuinness, two wins at 8f on good or soft, but his 2/29 trainer 14-day strike rate is modest; his best chance rests on dictating entirely unchallenged, which this field shape supports.|
runners_data.comment: Johnny Soda won last time out and also scored four starts back, a pattern of bouncing back well after blips, with today's trip already covered. Ranked only fourth on our figures, a below-par seventh two starts back is the main knock against him.

runners_data.name: Golddream
runners_data.note: David Marnane's prominent racer has a win at 8f on standard and a place on good, and Luke McAteer is a capable jockey to position him just off the pace; trainer has gone 0/14 in the past fortnight which is worth noting.|
runners_data.comment: Golddream won earlier in the campaign and already has today's trip covered. A below-par fifth last time is the main concern, but he rates our second-best and remains a real threat.

runners_data.name: Glitter And Glory
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington's runner has strong placed form on good ground (2nd at 8f, 2nd at 7f on good), travels prominently in her natural role, and has the most consistent profile of the prominent types behind the leader.|
runners_data.comment: Glitter And Glory was runner-up last time out and has today's trip covered, a consistent profile built on regular placed efforts. She rates our third-best; the main caveat is a yard currently out of form.

runners_data.name: Vishaya
runners_data.note: Style is unclassified, ridden by the talented Dylan Browne McMonagle for Joseph Patrick O'Brien whose yard is in fine form (14/53 in 14 days); form figures of 338 are modest but connections are of the quality to improve her on this track.|
runners_data.comment: Vishaya has place form to call on but dipped to eighth last time out, a mixed recent picture. A quick 19-day turnaround and an in-form yard are pluses; still winless of late and rated only sixth, she has questions to answer.

runners_data.name: Casamorati
runners_data.note: O'Brien's hold-up type is flagged as fading in finishes and returns after 69 days off; form figures of 689 show no encouragement, and the fade tendency is a genuine concern in a scenario that could compress finishes.|
runners_data.comment: Casamorati has faded across his last three starts — sixth, then eighth, then ninth last time out — and returns from a lengthy 69-day absence. His yard is in good form, though, and today's trip is proven ground for him, keeping this fifth-rated sort in the picture.

runners_data.name: Chirac
runners_data.note: Ronan Whelan takes the ride on this John James Feane runner who is genuinely prominent-natured but has been mapped to midfield given the crowded pace positions — his Killarney debut and trainer's modest 0/6 14-day record make him difficult to trust.|
runners_data.comment: Chirac returned to form when runner-up last time out and landed a win earlier in the campaign, and today's trip is covered. But a patchy sequence with unplaced runs in it makes him hard to trust, and he rates only our second-bottom here.

runners_data.name: Dervo Annie
runners_data.note: Claire O'Connell's mare has a win and multiple places in good-ground sprints and comes in on just 12 days' rest; front-running by nature, she is unlikely to get that position here and racing off the pace against her instincts is a significant ask.|
runners_data.comment: Dervo Annie was runner-up last time out and is quickly back after just 12 days, with today's trip already covered. Bottom of our figures, though, she has plenty to find to be involved at the finish.

races.paceDynamic: Johnny Soda is the confirmed front-runner and looks set to dictate from the front at a sustainable, uncontested gallop over this mile on good turf. With no genuine rival likely to press him early, he can control the tempo and present a flat, even pace scenario rather than a pressured slog. Dervo Annie and Chirac are both natural prominent types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map — this field contains more pace-seeking runners than can realistically secure those forward positions, and Glitter And Glory and Golddream are best-placed to actually occupy the prominent berths behind Johnny Soda. An uncontested, moderate pace over a flat mile on good ground typically sets up the race for horses travelling comfortably in the prominent-to-midfield bracket who have the turn of foot to quicken in the final two furlongs — hold-up horses face the risk of a late-arriving challenge that arrives too late if the winner kicks early from the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Soda Controls, Kick Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Johnny Soda dictates an uncontested pace and delivers a strong turning kick that holds all challengers at bay.
scenarios.body: Johnny Soda rolls along at his own tempo, and the steady early fractions mean those tracking him in the prominent positions — Glitter And Glory and Golddream — fire their challenges at the same time but find him hard to collar if he has conserved enough energy.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challengers Reel Him In
scenarios.trigger: If those travelling prominently behind Soda press at the two-furlong pole and the leader's early comfort is exposed.
scenarios.body: Glitter And Glory or Golddream, travelling sweetly just off the pace, unleash a sustained challenge that overcomes Johnny Soda inside the final furlong as the gallop has been just quick enough to expose any flat-spot in him.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race and the front rank ties up, allowing hold-up horses to arrive with a sweeping challenge.
scenarios.body: Red Autumn, dropping back from 9f and holding genuine good-ground form, and Vishaya, handled by Dylan Browne McMonagle with tactical nous, get a fast enough pace to reel off a strong late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos From Congestion
scenarios.trigger: If Dervo Annie or Chirac — both natural front-runners pushed into midfield — choose to force their way forward and create a contested, messy pace that scrambles the field.
scenarios.body: An unplanned pace-clash scrambles the shape entirely, burning off Johnny Soda and opening the race up to a surprise performer with hidden improvement — Casamorati or Vishaya could theoretically land in that vacuum, though both carry significant form questions at this level.

watchPoints.text: Johnny Soda — watch whether he is actively allowed to stride clear unchallenged from the gates, as any pressure from Chirac or Dervo Annie in the early stages would fundamentally alter this race shape.
Dervo Annie and Chirac — both natural front-runners, both mapped to midfield; if either forces forward at the break it could create an unplanned contested gallop that changes the complexion entirely.

Glitter And Glory — she has the most consistent prominent form on good ground in this field and if she travels smoothly just behind Johnny Soda she could be the most dangerous immediate pursuer in the final quarter mile.

Red Autumn — Sam Coen's 5lb claim is an asset, but watch whether the pace is genuinely strong enough to allow a hold-up horse to close; on a flat track at steady fractions she may simply never get into it.

Vishaya — Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking for an O'Brien runner with unclassified style could be significant if he decides to produce her with a forward move rather than waiting; her exact race position is the key variable.

races.name: Killarney Glamping Handicap

runners_data.name: Howyoulikethat
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse by nature who has finished placed off similar trips on Soft/Standard ground, but sim-going record of 0W1P from 15 matches at Good is uninspiring; 115 days off and a 5lb claimer in the saddle add further questions about readiness.
runners_data.comment: An in-the-frame third earlier in this sequence, plus today's trip already proven, underpin the case for this as our pick, even with results that read moderately on paper. A 115-day absence is the reservation, but a rating of 85 keeps the profile firmly in play.

runners_data.name: American Lawyer
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and returning after 335 days off the track for AJ Martin, whose yard is 1/8 over 14 days — the going is flagged unknown and this horse's running style is unclassified, making him a near-total unknown who must be treated with caution rather than confidence.
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced and hard to assess off a limited sample, with a third the best of its last five starts. Yet to win in that sequence, and a 335-day layoff adds further uncertainty, but there's scope for improvement as an unexposed sort.

runners_data.name: Quatre Bras
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter for this race, though his history shows he has predominantly raced at 10f-12f on Soft — dropping to a flat mile on Good ground is a significant profile shift, and a sim-going record of 0W0P from just 1 Good-ground run underscores the concern about him lasting home having made the running.
runners_data.comment: Today's trip is already proven and a runner-up effort earlier in this campaign points to real engine, backed by a rating of 86 — the highest of these. Two blank runs since are the worry, but a fresh 24-day gap gives this the chance to bounce back into contention.

runners_data.name: Earls
runners_data.note: Strong form at 8f on Good ground with two recent second-place finishes, and the tongue-tie is already applied — however, Gavin Cromwell's yard is 1/46 over 14 days, and as a genuine hold-up performer pushed into a midfield map role because the rear is crowded, his ability to get a clear run from his likely position is not guaranteed.
runners_data.comment: The last two starts have both been runner-up efforts, a marked step up on three below-par runs before, and a rating of 79 reflects that improving form. Today's trip is proven, though a yard currently out of form adds a note of caution.

runners_data.name: Molto Amichi
runners_data.note: A prominent racer who handles Good ground well — sim-going record of 0W5P from 11 Good-going runs shows consistent placing ability — and a step back from 9f-10f trips to one mile may sharpen his finishing effort if the pace is controlled.
runners_data.comment: A runner-up last time out, backed by another second and a third in the same sequence, underlines claims sharpened by a strong speed figure of 79. A ninth two starts back is the outlier, but proven form over today's trip keeps this among the leading dangers.

runners_data.name: Louiescall
runners_data.note: Returns after 268 days off but boasts a strong profile on Good ground over big distances, with 1W6P from 12 sim-going runs; runs prominently, which suits this shape well, though the fitness query after a long absence and a trainer strike rate of 0/11 over 14 days are tangible flags.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out to cap a solid run of form that also included a second and a fifth, with today's trip already proven. A 268-day absence since that success is the obvious concern, and a rating of 72 leaves this the outsider of the group.

runners_data.name: Marta's Prince
runners_data.note: A hold-up type who ran just 13 days ago and whose sim-going record on Good is 0W0P from 1 run — limited evidence he handles the ground, and finishing tailed off last time does not encourage confidence that he can pounce late from an already crowded rear group.
runners_data.comment: Well held in each of the last three starts, with the solitary win now four starts back, leaving little recent form to work with on a rating of 52. A brisk 13-day turnaround is a plus, but this looks the outsider of the group on recent evidence.

runners_data.name: Grey Leader
runners_data.note: Holds winning form on Good ground at 8f but has been well beaten in recent runs, and as a true closer who cannot get to the back of this field in the natural order of the race, his redistribution to a midfield slot means he is unlikely to be producing his running from his preferred position — the Burns yard is 0/6 over 14 days.
runners_data.comment: The bare results undersell this, with a rating of 83 and a speed figure of 81 hinting at more than the last five finishes show, plus today's trip is proven. A quick 13-day turnaround keeps this fresh, though finishing outside the frame every time is the knock.

races.paceDynamic: Quatre Bras is the one confirmed front-runner and will attempt to dictate from the outset at what should be a sustainable, uncontested gallop over this flat mile at Killarney. With Molto Amichi and Louiescall likely to press from prominent positions, Quatre Bras faces some company but nothing that should turn this into a true test of pace — a controlled tempo is the most probable outcome. The field holds more hold-up types than the shape can accommodate at the rear: Grey Leader and Earls are genuine closers by nature but are mapped to midfield because Howyoulikethat and Marta's Prince are also looking to come from off the pace, meaning the true hold-up brigade cannot all find their natural ground. This race shape — a lone leader setting a moderate, managed gallop with a compact midfield — will suit horses who can travel prominently and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out, giving the edge to Molto Amichi and Louiescall over the pure closers who may find the tempo insufficient to stretch the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Quatre Bras Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Quatre Bras gets a clean break and dictates a moderate pace unchallenged through the early stages.
scenarios.body: Quatre Bras sets a comfortable tempo that keeps the race together until the home straight, allowing prominent horses who track the leader to pounce at the right moment without burning energy chasing. Molto Amichi and Louiescall, both capable of racing prominently and sustaining a run, are ideally suited to latch on and pick off a front-runner who has had it too easy.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Louiescall and Molto Amichi both push forward and inject more tempo into the race, pressing Quatre Bras throughout.
scenarios.body: A contested pace develops with three horses fighting for supremacy up front, gradually increasing the gallop and stretching the field into a more strung-out shape. This opens the door for a horse with a genuine sustained gallop who can get into a rhythm — Louiescall, who has won and placed repeatedly over Good ground at big distances, may prove the strongest of the prominent group.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs or a contested early gallop empties the principals, leaving a vacancy for a horse coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Earls and Howyoulikethat, though both mapped closer than their natural rear position warrants, could still produce a late challenge if the race is truly run at a proper gallop that softens the front-runners late. The caveat is that Earls and Grey Leader in particular are not guaranteed to find their natural position in this shape, limiting the reliability of this outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Lands a Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run in unusual fashion — a false start, bunched field, or pace collapse — and an unexposed or lightly-raced runner finds gaps at the right moment.
scenarios.body: American Lawyer, lightly raced and unexposed after 335 days off, is the wildcard here — a completely unknown quantity whose form profile offers little read but whose freshness could be an asset if the race sets up unusually. Grey Leader, who has shown fleeting ability at this trip on Good ground, offers minimal each-way value in a race that does not naturally suit his profile.

watchPoints.text: Watch Quatre Bras's jumping-off speed at the start — if he doesn't break cleanly and establish the lead immediately, Louiescall or Molto Amichi could take over and fundamentally alter who is setting the tempo and at what gallop.

Grey Leader and Earls are both genuine hold-up horses forced into a midfield tactical position by the number of closers in the field — monitor whether either can work his way back to a true rail-saving position or whether they end up racing in too-prominent a spot for their style to work.

American Lawyer's unknown going preference and 335-day absence make him a live market mover to track in the ring — any significant support should be noted given AJ Martin's record of placing unexposed horses off long breaks.

Louiescall's 268-day break is a significant fitness query despite a strong Good-ground profile — watch whether connections have given him a prep workout or whether his conditioning is an unknown similar to American Lawyer's.

The going is recorded as unknown for all runners at Killarney today — if the track dries further ahead of the 7:00, horses with confirmed Good-ground form such as Earls (two recent seconds on Good) and Louiescall benefit, while Quatre Bras's Soft-biased history becomes a greater concern.

races.name: Kerry Publicans Summer Race Day Fillies Maiden
Irish Stallion Farms EBF Median Auction Maiden
Heights Hotel, Killarney Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Sands Castle
runners_data.note: Harry Sexton's 3yo hold-up type has placed once from six runs on similar going and steps up to 1m3½f; form figures of 2/10f/GOO suggest the trip and ground suit, but a high-draw in a big field means traffic management is crucial.
runners_data.comment: A runner-up last time out was the best of her recent starts, and a strong speed figure of 78 hints at more than bare results show — enough to top this line-up on a rating of 66. Today's trip is proven, though she is without a win in her last five.

runners_data.name: Sir Trancealot
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes the ride for JP Murtagh, whose stable is in strong form (7/32 in 14 days); a genuine hold-up performer with three runs at 12f+ on good ground, placing once, and headgear note (blinkers) may sharpen focus here.
runners_data.comment: A third two starts back is the form highlight, sandwiched by modest efforts either side, and a rating of 57 places this squarely in the pack. Today's trip is already proven and a swift 10-day turnaround helps, though nothing here demands respect above a midfield finish.

runners_data.name: Wipeawayyourtears
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner but officially tagged as a prominent horse racing out of that pure lead role; won last time over 12f on good and has placed twice from six on similar going — gets an uncontested lead here but STYLE_FIT of 0.93 is a mild caution on its true efficacy in a race that needs front-running.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, with a second and a third also banked in this sequence, suggesting a rating of 57 undersells the upward trend. A sixth and one finish outside the frame are the only blips, and a 31-day gap is the sole query.

runners_data.name: Chicago Moon
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's 3yo is a true hold-up horse pushed into a midfield map position by the volume of closers; ran once on good going without placing, but headgear (p) and a long 62-day absence since last run are notable flags — needs everything to go right in traffic.
runners_data.comment: A third three starts back is the standout in an otherwise indifferent sequence bookended by a ninth and a fifth, with a rating of 59 fitting a middling profile. Today's trip is proven, though a 62-day absence and modest recent efforts leave this needing to find more.

runners_data.name: Point Cartwright
runners_data.note: Ronan Whelan partners this prominent-racing McGuinness runner, placed twice from six at trip on good ground; ran just nine days ago so fitness is assured, and a willingness to race forward makes it one of the few horses likely to actually secure its natural position in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Placed in each of the last two starts — second then third — this looks the in-form threat here, aided by a swift 9-day turnaround and proven form over today's trip. A rating of 60 backs the case, though a string of minor honours is the one reservation.

runners_data.name: Guildhall Graduate
runners_data.note: Cromwell's hold-up performer has two entries in a 14-day window but only 1/46 strike rate — the horse's true style is at the rear, yet volume of closers pushes it into a midfield slot on the map; seven runs without a place on good ground is a concern.
runners_data.comment: The figures rate this well above its recent finishes, third in the field on a rating of 60 and a stronger speed figure of 68, with today's trip proven. A yard out of form is the concern, and a modest sequence — no better than fifth — remains the query.

runners_data.name: Cameclose
runners_data.note: Jack Davison's 3yo has a finish-fade flag and a redistribution note — naturally suited to holding up but mapped forward; placed once from seven on good going and ran 21 days ago, but the fade tendency at the business end limits confidence in any scenario that needs a late burst.
runners_data.comment: A runner-up last time out is the pick of a mixed sequence that's also featured two ninths, and a strong speed figure of 64 hints at more than a rating of 55 suggests. Today's trip is proven, but the inconsistency here is the obvious hold-up.

runners_data.name: Flagstone Lady
runners_data.note: Colin Keane in the saddle for a horse that fades in the finish and is redistributed from the rear to midfield; form of 8060 with no place in four runs on good ground makes this a significant ask, even with a top jockey booking.
runners_data.comment: Little in the recent form to shout about, with a best of sixth in the last four starts, and a rating of 48 near the bottom of the pack here. A 21-day turnaround at least keeps her fresh, but this looks a tough task on the evidence.

runners_data.name: Tintinabulla
runners_data.note: Lavery-trained 3yo has only three runs, all without placing and two on soft ground — the one run on good resulted in a last-of-field finish; the fade flag and a low sample on this going make it hard to assess with confidence.
runners_data.comment: Prop of the weights on a rating of 38, despite a notably stronger speed figure of 62 hinting at unrealised ability, with the last three starts yielding nothing better than a seventh. Today's trip is proven, but there's plenty to find on these figures.

runners_data.name: Augusta Rock
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's 3yo wears a visor and has been off 71 days — the longest absence in the field; four runs without a place including on good ground, and the STYLE_FIT tag means its mapped position overstates its likely finishing position.
runners_data.comment: A modest recent record — nothing better than eighth in the last four starts — leaves this towards the foot of the field on a rating of 44. A yard in good form is some encouragement, but a 71-day absence and the bare form make this hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: No Bother Aoife
runners_data.note: Cromwell's second string (1/46 14-day strike) wears a hood and fades in the finish; four runs on good going without a place and mapped away from its natural rear position — the redistribution note means it is unlikely to race where it needs to in order to be effective.
runners_data.comment: A fourth last time out is the best of a workmanlike sequence that's also brought two eighths, and a rating of 52 places this squarely mid-pack. Today's trip is proven and a swift 10-day turnaround helps, though a yard out of form is a mild concern.

runners_data.name: Polanco
runners_data.note: Three successive zeros in recent form and consistently runs out of the back on good ground; wears a tongue-tie and fades in the finish, making this a difficult proposition even in the most favourable scenario — redistribution means it won't get the hold-up berth it naturally seeks.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in each of the last four starts and only an eighth to show for the one before that, this sits towards the foot of the field on a rating of 46. A prompt 13-day turnaround is the only thing in this profile's favour.

runners_data.name: Stonyfalls
runners_data.note: Placed once from five on good ground over shorter trips (7-8f) and now steps up considerably in distance; Paul Traynor yard has a modest 14-day record and the fade flag adds doubt, though the extra yardage could theoretically unlock a new dimension.
runners_data.comment: A third last time out stands out in an otherwise modest sequence that's also brought two ninths, and a strong speed figure of 60 hints at more than a rating of 50 suggests. An 11-day turnaround keeps this fresh, but the inconsistency in the form is the query.

runners_data.name: Cadreville
runners_data.note: Neve Bennett (7lb claimer) partners a Fahey-trained filly who has placed once from six on good going; races over a longer trip than her best form and natural hold-up style is compromised by redistribution — the step up to 1m3½f is unproven.
runners_data.comment: A much stronger speed figure of 57 outpaces a rating of only 42, with a third two starts back the best of a mixed sequence. A brisk 9-day turnaround and proven form over today's trip are the plus points, but the bare results keep this among the outsiders.

runners_data.name: Canon Law
runners_data.note: Brendan Duke's 3yo is a hold-up runner with a STYLE_FIT of 0.91, mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear; six runs on varying surfaces without a win and five successive out-of-the-frame efforts on Tapeta make the good-ground turf switch hard to assess.
runners_data.comment: A quick 9-day turnaround and proven form over today's trip give this the edge on conditions, with a rating of 63 backing the case despite a modest recent sequence — two sixths and a fifth the best of it. The fundamentals here, rather than outright form, make this our pick.

races.paceDynamic: Wipeawayyourtears is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner 1m3½f handicap and, with no genuine rival pressing for the lead, Jack Cleary's mount should dictate a controlled, measured gallop from the front — a pace that is sustainable rather than scorching. The bulk of the field is made up of hold-up types, but the race contains significantly more pace than the map can accommodate: Polanco, No Bother Aoife, Guildhall Graduate and Point Cartwright are all genuine prominent or hold-up runners who will be competing for early berths, and the most likely to actually secure a forward position are Point Cartwright and Polanco, who have both shown a willingness to race prominently when conditions allow. With a modest, unhurried gallop likely from the front, those sitting just behind the leader in the stalking position — close enough to the tempo to dictate when they pounce — are best placed, rather than deep closers who will face a wall of horses with nowhere to go in a compact handicap field. This race shape strongly favours hold-up-to-prominent stalkers with a genuine turn of foot at this trip on good ground, not the outright leaders or the deepest closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wipeawayyourtears Dictates Steadily
scenarios.trigger: If Wipeawayyourtears goes unchallenged and sets a controlled, even gallop that rewards those tracking close behind.
scenarios.body: Wipeawayyourtears controls the tempo and the race becomes a test of which stalker can produce the sharpest acceleration in the straight; horses sitting second or third with cover are ideally placed as the pace is never truly punishing. Point Cartwright, who has placed twice at this trip on good ground and races prominently, is the profile that benefits most from this shape alongside any horse who can settle just off the leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a horse settles just off the lead in a clear position and produces a decisive burst when Wipeawayyourtears ties up in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: The modest gallop lures the field into a false sense of comfort before the straight, where a horse with a clean passage and tactical pace delivers the winning thrust past a tiring leader. Sir Trancealot, proven at the trip on good ground with a strong jockey booking in Ben Coen, and Point Cartwright are the profiles most suited to this outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and a genuine closer finds daylight to run through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires a true staying closer to pick a path through a packed field as front-runners empty — possible but mechanically difficult given the sheer number of hold-up types redistributed from the rear, meaning traffic is the principal danger. Sands Castle, who has finishing form at the trip on good going, and Chicago Moon carry the right profile, though both face congestion risk given the field size.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Collapse — Winner From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace suddenly quickens mid-race, stringing the field out and allowing a hold-up horse to pick off tiring rivals in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape because the majority of hold-up types are not true deep closers in this race and many carry STYLE_FIT or REDISTRIBUTED tags, meaning their natural finishing kick is overstated by their map position. Only a genuinely unfortunate set of circumstances — a false jump or a mid-race injection of pace — would gift the rail-skimmers a winning opportunity here.

watchPoints.text: Wipeawayyourtears — if anything challenges for the lead in the first furlong, the pace could inflate sharply, completely changing the race shape and bringing hold-up horses back into contention; watch the early exchanges closely to see if it gets a true solo lead.

Point Cartwright and Polanco — both will attempt to claim a forward position and if they crowd the leader early, the tactical race becomes more attritional than expected, which could inconvenience horses tracking just behind.

Traffic danger for all hold-up types in the final two furlongs — with so many closers mapped to midfield and the rear, the straight at Killarney over this trip is likely to be extremely congested; horses without a clean run could find their challenge materially impeded.

Augusta Rock (71 days off, visor) and Chicago Moon (62 days off) are the two longest-absent runners — note whether either is being given a school or is genuinely primed for a peak effort, as trainer intentions will be difficult to read in-running.

Ben Coen's booking for Sir Trancealot (JP Murtagh yard in strong form at 7/32) is the standout jockey-trainer angle in the race and worth monitoring in the market to see whether it is attracting support consistent with stable confidence.
